goal: WAVE 5: finish every buildable gap with real backend integration on Nano + offline (config_only enforced, buildable not_simulated built, engine-coverage limits lifted)
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/monitor.json (38 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Alerts, Metrics, Observability agents (preview), Issues, Logs, Health models, Change Analysis, Service health, Workbooks, Dashboards with Grafana, Insights, Managed Services)
Backend: core azure monitor (test_azure_monitor_core.py, test_azure_operationalinsights_core.py): metrics, activity log, alerts, Log Analytics query if modeled
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/monitor.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.monitor.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: Per-resource-type Insights dashboards (Applications, Virtual Machines, Storage accounts, Networks, Azure Cosmos DB, Key Vaults, Service Bus)
limitations: Shows Vyomi's real resource inventory for the type; there is no request/exception/dependency telemetry, VM guest metrics, or health rollup — those need an agent-based collection pipeline Vyomi does not run.

depth_targets.title: Metrics — scope picker (resource types, locations)
limitations: Scope, resource-type and location pickers are real (drawn from your inventory); the chart itself is not — metric definitions/values are not modelled.

depth_targets.title: Monitoring Coverage (resources with vs. without an alert rule)
limitations: Coverage is approximated as "referenced by at least one alert rule's scopes"; Azure's own per-signal telemetry coverage model is not reproduced.

depth_targets.title: Advisor recommendations (resources with no alert rule, derived from real inventory)
limitations: Recommendations are "this resource has no alert rule", not Azure Advisor's own usage-pattern heuristics.

depth_targets.title: Metrics charts (metric definitions and time-series values)
limitations: Metric definitions and metric values are not modelled — there is no time-series store to chart.
Not simulated: Scope, Metric Namespace, Metric, Aggregation, Add metric, Add filter, Apply splitting, Line chart, Drill into Logs, New alert rule, Save to dashboard.

depth_targets.title: Log Analytics query (KQL)
limitations: Only a small KQL subset is understood: a table name, then any of where (==/!=/contains/startswith), project, sort by/order by, take/limit and count — unsupported syntax returns a real error instead of succeeding silently.

Only the built-in AzureActivity table has rows, and they are the subscription's real Activity log (the same Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes feed the Activity log page reads) — every other table (Heartbeat, Perf, Syslog, Event, Usage, AzureDiagnostics, any custom _CL/_RST table) is always empty: there is no agent/telemetry ingestion pipeline.

AzureActivity is not gated by a per-workspace Activity Log export / diagnostic setting (Vyomi does not model one at subscription scope) — every workspace's AzureActivity table sees the whole subscription feed.

The api.loganalytics.io data-plane host itself (azure-monitor-query / LogsQueryClient) is not modelled; the query runs over the same ARM pass-through path (.../workspaces/{ws}/api/query) the Azure Portal's Logs blade uses.

depth_targets.title: Observability agents (preview)
limitations: Agent-based collector management is out of scope for a simulator.

depth_targets.title: Issues
limitations: Cross-signal issue correlation is not modelled.

depth_targets.title: Health models
limitations: Health model authoring and evaluation is not modelled.

depth_targets.title: Change Analysis (derived from the real Activity log)
limitations: Change type/Name/Resource type are derived from the Activity log feed (real ARM writes), not from Azure Resource Graph's property-level snapshots — there is no before/after diff of individual properties.
Toolbar actions not simulated: Open query, Group by none.

depth_targets.title: Service health
limitations: There is no Azure service-health incident feed to mirror; every simulated service is always healthy.

depth_targets.title: Dashboards with Grafana
limitations: Azure Managed Grafana is a separate managed service Vyomi does not run.
Toolbar actions would be New, Explore, Browse Grafana dashboards Gallery, Browse Saved dashboards, Help, Feedback, Group by.

depth_targets.title: Container insights
limitations: AKS/ACI are not modelled by any Vyomi core, so there is no container inventory to show.

depth_targets.title: Azure Cache for Redis insights
limitations: Azure Cache for Redis is not modelled by any Vyomi core.

depth_targets.title: Azure Data Explorer Clusters insights
limitations: Azure Data Explorer is not modelled by any Vyomi core.

depth_targets.title: Azure Local insights
limitations: Azure Local (hybrid hardware) is out of scope for a cloud simulator.

depth_targets.title: Managed Prometheus
limitations: Azure Kubernetes Service and the managed Prometheus add-on are not modelled.
Grid columns would be Name, Resource group, Metrics collection; toolbar actions would be View manual setup, Feedback.

depth_targets.title: Azure Managed Grafana
limitations: Azure Managed Grafana is a separate managed service Vyomi does not run.

depth_targets.title: Azure Monitor SCOM managed instance
limitations: SCOM managed instance is out of scope for a simulator.

depth_targets.title: Diagnostic settings (per-resource logs/metrics routing: resource picker + create/list/delete)
limitations: Logs/metrics are never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline, so the setting is stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires but nothing flows.

Vyomi has no catalog of a resource type's real log/metric category names (GET .../diagnosticSettingsCategories is not modelled) — the create form offers the 'allLogs' category group and 'AllMetrics' rather than a resource-specific category picker.

depth_targets.title: Azure Monitor pipelines
limitations: Azure Monitor pipelines (on-premises collector fleet management) are out of scope for a simulator.

depth_targets.title: Azure Monitor Private Link Scopes (create, list, delete, access mode settings)
limitations: The scope resource and its query/ingestion access-mode settings are real and round-trip exactly as configured; private endpoint connections and scoped-resource associations (linking workspaces/App Insights components into the scope) are not modelled — Vyomi has no private networking stack.

depth_targets.title: New support request (file a Microsoft support ticket)
limitations: Vyomi does not file real Microsoft support tickets.

DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

WAVE 5 — FINISH THE GAPS (orchestrator). Work through EVERY entry in depth_targets in this order:
  1. config_only → make the stored setting TAKE EFFECT (e.g. encryption really uses our KMS / Key Vault cores; access logging really writes log objects; org-policy constraints really reject violating calls; tiering/lifecycle really moves objects; replication really copies within the simulator). Raise to limited/full.
  2. not_simulated that a simulator CAN model → build it in the shared core (state + native API + console + smoke round-trip + conformance test). Networking behaviour MUST use core/netsim (never a second evaluator).
  3. limited whose limit is only missing engine coverage (query grammar, per-request policy evaluation, missing sub-resources) → lift it.
  KEEP HONEST only: separate products (Grafana, Prometheus, Defender, Bastion, VPN/TGW/ExpressRoute, PrivateLink, Firehose without a core…), billing/payment/support, physical hardware, AI-generated insights — with the concrete reason in `limitations`.
Both substrates: every change must work on Nano (wasm cores) AND offline (check the offline route serves it — offline sometimes uses legacy provider handlers; route to the core or implement there; see core/wire_ingress.py, providers/*, routes/*). New offline state must be durable (core/appliance_stores._CoreSlotStore) and JSON-safe. Run the gate, the cloud's smoke, and the conformance tests in the FOREGROUND before your final message; commit source.
